differences: Numbers that did not reproduce (the converted rows are unchanged): motor noise sigma_m (SD of reach angles, outliers removed), mean over participants, deg: 3.015 here, 2.98 in the paper (Results, motor-awareness task (sigma_m mean 2.98 deg)). sigma_m SD across participants, deg: 1.184 here, 1.26 in the paper (Results, motor-awareness task (SD 1.26)). points earned, SD across participants: 1018.607 here, 1018 in the paper (Results, task performance (SD 1018)).

The authors' code calls the 20 deg rotation of blocks 1 and 3 'rotate left'. The stored angles are computed from screen pixels with y down, so adding 20 deg turns the feedback clockwise on the screen; this file records the rotation by that screen geometry (-20 deg in counter-clockwise-positive terms in blocks 1 and 3). Each rotated block is mirrored in the authors' own analysis (LSoutMatGen.m multiplies odd blocks by -1), so their figures are unaffected.

Unlike the implicit-adaptation deposit, reportAngle is not negated here: it is saved as the plain angle of the reported point and the authors' scripts use it as reportAngle - 90, which hand_report keeps.

The paper says the motor-awareness task gave no feedback on experimental trials (only on practice trials), although the control-task code has a feedback screen; the rows follow the paper (fb_visible none).
The paper replaced one outlying feedback error and one confidence report of one participant before fitting; the rows here keep the raw values.
